budget.method: budget: the operator's total, set in the first-run wizard (default 20 GB, published). spend: the lane file on disk including its -wal/-shm sidecars. rate is the collection-speed governor's, not a second budget.

rows_per_day.method: versioned_changes rows, grouped by the day THIS APP recorded them (not the day the edit happened -- a resumed stream replays yesterday)
rows_per_day.caveat: A day inside the window with no rows is a real zero for that day; the block reports measured:false only when the whole window is empty.

bytes_per_day.method: the lane file on disk (stat + -wal/-shm), sampled at most hourly
bytes_per_day.caveat: Measured between the first and last samples in this window only. A lane that was stopped for part of it grew for less time than the span suggests, and this figure does not know that.

gaps.method: versioned_gaps rows the lane wrote itself, newest first
gaps.caveat: A gap says a stretch of the change log was not handed to this app. It is never a percentage: a lane cannot know how much it missed, only that it missed a named stretch.

entities.method: versioned_entities rows, grouped by the reason each was admitted
entities.caveat: 'unrecorded' means the row predates the column, not that no rule applied.

lane_counters.method: Composed from rows the lane already wrote -- there is no counters file. Every block survives a restart, because nothing here is a process-cumulative counter.

bar: every figure above is read from the lane's own rows; the resolution count is taken at socket.getaddrinfo, because a DNS lookup is itself egress
